---
title: "Homozygosity under selfing"
description: "How quickly lines from a cross become homozygous with each generation of self-pollination."
---

## The idea

An F~1~ from a cross between two homozygous parents is heterozygous at every locus where the parents differ. Each generation of self-pollination halves the proportion of heterozygous loci. In generation F~*g*~, the expected proportion of loci that are still heterozygous is

$$
H_g = \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{g-1},
$$

so the proportion homozygous is 1 − *H*~*g*~. For a single plant to be homozygous at **all** *n* independent segregating loci, the probability is

$$
\Pr(\text{fully homozygous in } F_g) = \left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{g-1}\right]^{n}.
$$

The first expression does not depend on how many loci are segregating. The second does, strongly, which is why lines from a wide cross still segregate for some traits after several generations of selfing.

*Source: Fehr, Principles of Cultivar Development, Vol. 1, chapters 2–3.*

## Widget

```{ojs}
viewof nLoci = Inputs.range([1, 100], {value: 10, step: 1, label: "Segregating loci (n)"})
viewof gen = Inputs.range([2, 12], {value: 6, step: 1, label: "Generation (F)"})
```

```{ojs}
rows = d3.range(1, 13).flatMap(g => {
  const homLoci = 1 - 0.5 ** (g - 1);
  return [
    {g, value: homLoci, measure: "Loci homozygous (average)"},
    {g, value: homLoci ** nLoci, measure: `Plants homozygous at all ${nLoci} loci`}
  ];
})
current = rows.filter(d => d.g === gen)
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  height: 340,
  marginLeft: 50,
  x: {label: "Generation", ticks: 12, tickFormat: d => `F${d}`},
  y: {label: "Proportion", domain: [0, 1], grid: true, tickFormat: "%"},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(rows, {x: "g", y: "value", stroke: "measure", strokeWidth: 2, marker: "circle"}),
    Plot.ruleX([gen], {strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.text(current, {x: "g", y: "value", text: d => `${(d.value * 100).toFixed(1)}%`, dx: 8, textAnchor: "start"})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
md`In **F${gen}**, an average line is homozygous at **${(current[0].value * 100).toFixed(1)}%** of its segregating loci, but only **${(current[1].value * 100).toFixed(1)}%** of plants are homozygous at all ${nLoci} loci.`
```

## Things to try

- With *n* = 1 the two curves are the same. Raise *n* and watch the second curve slide to the right.
- Find the generation where at least half of the plants are fully homozygous for *n* = 20, then for *n* = 100.
- Breeders often call F~5~ or F~6~ lines "essentially homozygous". Check what that means for 50 segregating loci.
